keys.unit: a tie: a respondent (US adult) and one of up to ten people named as someone they discuss important matters with or who is most significant to them
keys.relation: partner, child, parent, sibling, other family, non-kin; co-worker, neighbour, group member, online are overlapping flags
keys.distance: nine bands as asked, in miles

envelope.ties: closest ties only, at most ten; 14 % of respondents named nobody

tags.may_last: where closest ties live, by relation (T1); the in-person gradient
tags.a_2008_price_not_to_be_carried: each level of electronic contact, the mix of means, and the bridge shares in T3

who_is_missing: 58 % of partnered respondents named a partner at home; named co-resident adults are 47 % of the other adults at home and named children 16 % of the children at home. Household rows are given as named (a floor) and with unnamed co-residents added at the contact of named ones (a ceiling).

verdict.household_share_of_electronic_contact: at least 0.29 as named (met against a bar of 0.15); 0.52 to 0.61 with unnamed co-residents
verdict.written_contact_nearer_than_ties: neither met nor killed: 0.03 to 0.06 nearer, with gaps as large
verdict.relation_beyond_distance: neither: the total is the same for kin and non-kin at 5 to 50 miles; the mix is not (kin by voice, non-kin in writing)
verdict.all_rows: readings of a reference; no generator scored
